title: SpaceX and Tesla Stock Plunges Have Wiped About $450 Billion in Value Since the Midterms. Is It Time to Buy?
detail:
SpaceX and Tesla Stock Plunges Have Wiped About $450 Billion in Value Since the Midterms. Is It Time to Buy?
Jonathan Ponciano, The Motley Fool
Thu, November 5, 2026 at 1:03 PM PST 5 min read
TSLA
SPCX
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The two companies helmed by the world's richest person have had a rough two-day stretch on the market. Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) closed at $398.50 on Election Day, and by 3:08 p.m. ET Thursday, it was trading at about $342, down 14%, representing a loss of about $225 billion in market value. SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) fell from $141.31 to about $125, down 12%, or about $227 billion. Together, that's about $450 billion gone in two sessions, most of it on Thursday, when Tesla fell about 11% and SpaceX about 8%.

To illustrate how steep the drop has been, SpaceX is now trading below its $135 IPO price from June.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Why They're Falling

If you had to sum it up in one word: politics. Democrats now control both chambers of Congress, and Musk, a top ally of President Donald Trump, is a likely target. Speaking on the All-In podcast on election night, Texas Republican Sen. Ted Cruz said Democrats had signaled they would use subpoenas "to go after Elon Musk." In Texas, home to both companies, voters elected a Democratic attorney general for the first time since 1994.

But political sentiment isn't the only reason. The Nasdaq was headed for its worst day in 18 months on Thursday as investors dumped chip and data-center stocks, on fears that new leaders in Washington and the states could slow data-center construction. SpaceX, of course, is exposed: Last month, it committed to a roughly $40 billion lease for AI chips with an entity managed by Apollo Global Management, with payments starting in the first half of 2027.

Adding to the fire for SpaceX, Wall Street is reportedly trying to sell off pieces of that $40 billion chip deal to other investors, with Goldman Sachs and Apollo leading the effort, according to Bloomberg on Thursday.

The Case for SpaceX

SpaceX made money last quarter: $2.79 billion in operating income and $4.4 billion in net income, though it's still $413 million in the red for the first nine months of the year. Nothing that happened in Washington this week changes its launch business or Starlink.

But the fine print, or at least the filing details, are worth noting. That net income included a $390 million tax benefit and a $561 million unrealized gain on its stake in the Boring Company, Musk's tunneling firm, and two customers made up about half of quarterly revenue. Even after the drop, SpaceX is valued at about $1.7 trillion, roughly 150 times its third-quarter operating income on an annualized basis.

From a $17 IPO to a $1.52 Trillion AI Pivot

Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) went public on June 29, 2010, at $17 per share. It was a niche EV maker that much of Wall Street treated as a science project. Then came the Model S (2012), the mass-market Model 3 (2017), and the Model Y (2020), and each one drove Tesla closer to volume manufacturing.

jetcityimage / iStock Editorial via Getty Images

2020 was the turning point. Tesla joined the S&P 500, posted its first full year of profit, and split its stock 5-for-1 in August 2020, followed by a 3-for-1 split in August 2022.

Price Wars Gave Way to Robots and Robotaxis

In 2023 and 2024, price wars squeezed margins, and Elon Musk started talking far more about AI. That shift now shows up in the products. Robotaxi runs in 7 U.S. metros, Cybercab joined the fleet on Sept. 3, 2026, and Optimus production has started in Fremont. Tesla is worth $1.52 trillion.

Your $1,000 Turned Into About $241,852

Tesla has never paid a dividend, so every dollar of gain comes from the stock's rise. From the split-adjusted close on its first trading day ($1.59) to the $385.19 close on Nov. 4, $1,000 grew to $241,852.20. That is a 24,085.22% gain, or about 39.9% a year. Anyone who got shares at the $17 IPO price did even better.

title: Tesla Sinks 12%, SpaceX Down 9% as Midterm Sweep Puts Merger on “A Much Tougher Regulatory Roadmap”

SPCX

Trading disclosure
Tesla Sinks 12%, SpaceX Down 9% as Midterm Sweep Puts Merger on "A Much Tougher Regulatory Roadmap" ©TIKR

[IMAGE CREDIT: NASA/Aubrey Gemignani via Canva]

Key Takeaways

Tesla shares fell 12% today, and SpaceX fell too, after Democrats swept Congress and Texas and raised doubts about a SpaceX-Tesla merger.

A slower merger takes away part of the case Tesla's bulls have made since October.

Analysts expect normalized EPS of $3.24 in 2028, still below 2022's $4.07, so investors are paying mostly for Robotaxi, Optimus and the merger.

Even after the drop, Tesla trades far above its five-year average forward P/E.

Tesla (TSLA:NASDAQ) sank another 12% today. That adds to Wednesday's slide, which came after Democrats won the House, the Senate and the governor's office in Texas. Both Tesla and SpaceX (SPCX:NASDAQ) are headquartered in Texas.

A slower road to a merger

SpaceX fell 9% as well. On SpaceX's third-quarter call last month, Musk said merging the two would be a good idea, and both companies are exploring a deal.

Dan Ives is a partner and managing director at Yorkville and one of Wall Street's best-known Tesla bulls. He still expects a merger. But he wrote today that it "now faces a much tougher regulatory roadmap to get this deal done in 2027 given this new political blue roadmap in DC/Texas."

That's a problem for Tesla's bulls. When Barclays upgraded Tesla in late October, it called the merger a key part of the bull case and raised its target to $450.

Priced for Robotaxi, Optimus and the deal

You can't justify Tesla's price on its car and battery earnings alone. Analysts expect normalized EPS of $3.24 in 2028, which is still below the $4.07 Tesla earned in 2022:

Tesla (TSLA): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2023-2028 (TIKR)

Even so, Tesla's forward P/E stood at 189x before today's drop, far above its five-year average of 108x:

Tesla (TSLA): forward (NTM) P/E, last 5 years (TIKR)

At today's price, it's still about 170x. That's the kind of multiple AI stocks get, which helps explain why Tesla fell with chip and data-center stocks today.

TIKR tracks 44 analysts on Tesla. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Tesla, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Tesla's Analyst Ratings

Data-center power took a hit too

Bloom Energy (BE:NYSE) sank 17%, even though NTT DATA announced a 900 MW fuel cell deal with Bloom this morning. Goldman Sachs analysts expect Democratic wins at the state and local level to bring "short-term data center moratoria, potentially affecting about 45% of planned US data center capacity expansion."

That's a risk for Tesla too. Its energy business brought in 22% of the company's gross profit in 2025. And Morgan Stanley autos analyst Andrew Percoco just called Tesla the "very obvious player" in data-center batteries.

The firm more than doubled its Lucid (LCID) stake, lifting it 106% to 4.25 million shares from 2.06 million as of Q2-end.

The firm also sold its small stake in Faraday Future in the quarter.

Among Chinese EV makers, Citi added more Nio shares, while slashing its stake in XPeng and Li Auto.

Citigroup raised its stake in Tesla (TSLA) and a few other automakers in the third quarter, while cutting its stake in others including General Motors (GM) and XPeng (XPEV), according to a new filing.

The firm increased its Tesla common-stock holding 10.1% to 8.69 million shares, worth roughly $3.09 billion at the quarter-end. That compared with about 7.9 million shares valued near $3.32 billion three months earlier. The equity rise occurred even as the shares fell over the quarter, leaving the position's market value down about 7%.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

RIVN, LCID See Additions

Citigroup more than doubled its Lucid (LCID) stake, lifting it 106% to 4.25 million shares from 2.06 million as of Q2-end. The position's value still climbed only about 25% to $17.3 million because the stock dropped in the timeframe.

The firm's Rivian (RIVN) stake rose 39.7%to 8.56 million shares, partially reversing a second-quarter cut and leaving the holding just below levels reported at the end of March. The firm also sold its small stake in Faraday Future in the quarter.

Mixed Moves On Chinese EVs And Legacy Carmakers

Citigroup raised its Nio ADS holding 20% to 816,755 in the quarter.

By contrast, the bank reduced its XPeng holding 82.6% to 235,012 ADS and trimmed Li Auto holdings 20.1% to 2.23 million ADS, which remained its largest Chinese EV equity position at about $25.3 million.

Citigroup's Ford stake grew 31% to 13.05 million, while General Motors holdings declined 5% to 1.70 million.

Citigroup's overall reported holdings edged up to about $308.3 billion from $302.7 billion the prior quarter.

How Did TSLA Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around TSLA stock was 'extremely bearish' at the time of writing, while retail chatter stayed at 'normal' levels. Sentiment around RIVN, meanwhile, trended in the 'extremely bullish' territory.

TSLA stock has dropped 24% year-to-date.
